clue.text: Was it the glasshouse for William the Silent?

definitions.text: Was it the glasshouse for William the Silent?

parts.words: Was it the glasshouse for William the Silent?
parts.note: William the Silent was Prince of Orange, so his glasshouse is jokingly the one named after his house, a building for growing citrus trees

explanation.surface: A historical question about where a Dutch prince kept his plants.
explanation.walkthrough: William the Silent led the Dutch revolt as Prince of Orange; the answer is a heated garden house for citrus, read as if it belonged to the House of Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatory built for growing citrus trees through the winter is the kind of glasshouse meant.

clue.text: Peculiar condition of the man left out?

definitions.text: Peculiar condition of the man left out?

parts.words: Peculiar condition of the man left out?
parts.note: the one left out is the odd man out, and being odd is his condition, a strangeness

explanation.surface: Asking what is strange about the one excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'man left out' is the odd man out; his condition is being odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangeness or a strange feature is a peculiar condition.

clue.text: Hard-working duo is USA's, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be put another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of American workers described as diligent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging DUO IS USAS, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: Assiduous means diligent and persevering, the sense of hard-working.

clue.text: Enchantment of girl's initial love for Louis

indicators.note: initial means only the first letter of girl is taken

parts.note: l'amour is French for love, Louis being a typical Frenchman

explanation.surface: A girl's first romance with a Frenchman is magical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louis' stands for any Frenchman, so his word for love is L'AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour originally meant a magic spell, and still means alluring charm or enchantment.

clue.text: Produce straight lines, say

indicators.note: say means the word for straight lines is spoken aloud, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: rays are straight lines radiating from a point

explanation.surface: An instruction to draw some ruled lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' is a verb, as in rearing crops or children.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise crops or a family is to grow or produce them.

clue.text: Keen old bird in mountainous surroundings

indicators.note: the bird is placed inside the surrounding mountain word

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, here wrapped around the bird
the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: An extinct bird sits enclosed by high peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' is a verb here, to wail in mourning, not the adjective eager. BEN is a Scottish word for a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, the same as lamenting a loss.

clue.text: Seeks to justify makeshift substitutes

definitions.meaning: a verb: to defend or explain away a fault
a noun: poor stand-ins, as in 'a poor ... for a meal'

explanation.surface: Someone defending their use of improvised replacements.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for pleading justification and a plural noun for inadequate stand-ins.

clue.text: Son abandons prayer to the stars

indicators.note: abandons means the letter for son leaves the word for prayer

parts.note: an orison is an old word for a prayer

explanation.surface: A son stops praying and looks up to the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: ORISON is an archaic word for a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion, the hunter, is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: No point to mental perception associated with Lear?

parts.note: N is north, a point of the compass
sense is perception or understanding

explanation.surface: Questioning whether King Lear lacked mental awareness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's mad king, but it is Edward Lear, writer of comic verse such as A Book of Nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was famous for his comic absurd verse, the genre his name is tied to.

clue.text: Malefactor hurting our feelings?

definitions.meaning: read as one who is hurting, or causing upset to, us

explanation.surface: A villain upsetting everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a lawbreaker and anyone who gives affront.

clue.text: Boy rejected compensation, giving cause for complaint

indicators.note: rejected means the boy's name is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: Sid is a boy's name
satisfaction is redress or compensation for a wrong

explanation.surface: A lad turns down an offer of redress, which leads to a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SID round to DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is what gives someone grounds to grumble.

clue.text: A future wooer, he, regardless of maternal approval?

definitions.text: A future wooer, he, regardless of maternal approval?

parts.words: A future wooer, he, regardless of maternal approval?
parts.note: alludes to the nursery song in which a frog would a-wooing go whether his mother would let him or no; the answer is the young creature that later becomes that frog

explanation.surface: A suitor-to-be who will court regardless of his mother's say-so.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'A Frog He Would A-Wooing Go' has the frog go courting 'whether his mother would let him or no'; a future frog is its larva.
explanation.definitionFit: The larval stage of a frog is the creature that will grow into the rhyme's courting amphibian.

clue.text: In reality, an alcoholic solution

definitions.meaning: the phrase 'in ...' means fundamentally, in real terms, so the word stands for underlying reality
an extract of a plant's flavour dissolved in alcohol, as in vanilla extract

explanation.surface: A remark that, truth be told, the answer to things is drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the true inner nature of something and a flavouring extract dissolved in spirit.

clue.text: Glutton extremely glad to accommodate literary agent in Cuba?

indicators.note: to accommodate means the first and last letters of glad hold the agent inside them
extremely means take only the outermost letters of the word glad

parts.note: Graham Greene's novel Our Man in Havana is about a British agent in Cuba

explanation.surface: A big eater is happy to put up a spy from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely glad' gives G and D; 'to accommodate' puts OUR MAN between them. 'literary agent' looks like a publisher's agent, but it is the spy of Greene's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is one who eats greedily and to excess.

clue.text: Air may be pronounced so clear

definitions.meaning: air sounds like heir, and an heir may be 'heir ...', the one certain to inherit

explanation.surface: A tune may be declared plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'air' sounds like 'heir', and the phrase heir apparent is the certain successor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means plainly visible, and also the title of an heir whose succession is certain.

clue.text: Transatlantic uncle thus returned to an Aegean island

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States, across the Atlantic

indicators.note: returned means the word for thus is read backwards

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: An American relative travels back to a Greek isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SO round to OS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean, birthplace of Pythagoras.

clue.text: Old. Russia detailed with difficulty to produce sugar

indicators.note: detailed means the word loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: Muscovy is the old name for the Russian state centred on Moscow
ado is trouble or fuss

explanation.surface: An itemised account of old Russian hardship ending in sugar production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'itemised', but means de-tailed: MUSCOVY loses its last letter to make MUSCOV.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an unrefined brown cane sugar.

clue.text: Fighter managed to be in film — he moved overseas

indicators.note: to be in means the fighter and managed words go inside the film title

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
ran means managed, as in ran a shop

explanation.surface: A soldier who ran things in a movie later left the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' looks like a boxer or soldier; it is the Russian jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves to settle abroad has moved overseas.

clue.text: Noted provision for Orsino's conjectural agape?

definitions.text: Noted provision for Orsino's conjectural agape?

parts.words: Noted provision for Orsino's conjectural agape?
parts.note: Orsino opens Twelfth Night with 'If ... be the food of love, play on'; agape is love, the 'if' makes it conjectural, and the food is made of notes

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean duke speculates about feeding love.
explanation.walkthrough: Agape is Greek for love, not 'open-mouthed'. Orsino's line 'If music be the food of love' makes the answer love's possible food, a provision of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound arranged in notes is what Orsino imagines feeding his love on.

clue.text: Fast horse for a sheep-shearer?

definitions.meaning: a swift horse, by the same idea as the fast sailing ship
one who clips fleeces, or the shears used

explanation.surface: A speedy mount suitable for a farmhand at shearing time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a swift horse or ship, and also anyone or anything that cuts wool.

clue.text: Despair a worry? Not here, surely

indicators.note: to worry something is to tear and shake it about, so these letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A consoling thought that despair and anxiety will not be found in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worry' is the anagram signal on DESPAIR A. The definition is a joke: wherever the answer is, it is surely not on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is the place of bliss, supposedly never found in this world.

clue.text: Pooter, for one, said it badly? About right

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the letter for right
badly signals that the letters of said it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A comic character who misspoke and then got it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles SAID IT to DIAIST, and 'About' wraps that round R. Charles Pooter is the author of the comic diary in The Diary of a Nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooter keeps a daily journal in the Grossmiths' novel, so he is a journal-keeper.

clue.text: Directions' taken by Obadiah Slope

definitions.meaning: Slope is a clergyman in Trollope's Barchester Towers, so he has taken holy ones

explanation.surface: Instructions accepted by a Victorian novel's clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Obadiah Slope is the oily chaplain in Trollope's Barchester Towers; clergy 'take holy orders'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means commands, and the holy rank conferred at ordination.

clue.text: Workman less industrious after midnight

indicators.note: after means the slacker word follows the midnight letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night
lazier means less hard-working

explanation.surface: A labourer who slacks off more once the clock strikes twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', its letter G, not twelve o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits panes of glass is a kind of workman.

clue.text: Change in local terrain

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words local terrain

explanation.surface: A shift in the lie of the land nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to make or become different.

clue.text: Distinctive quality of popularly approved student

indicators.note: popular means in, so a popularly approved student is one placed in favour

parts.note: favour is approval, as in finding favour
L is the learner or student, from L-plates

explanation.surface: A pupil who is generally well liked has a certain character.
explanation.walkthrough: IN means popular, so 'popularly approved student' says the student is in favour: L goes inside FAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic taste or tone is a distinctive quality.

clue.text: Everyone in the sporting association is a composer

indicators.note: in means everyone is put inside the association's initials

parts.note: FA is the Football Association
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole football body turns out to be a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel de Falla wrote The Three-Cornered Hat, so he is a composer.

clue.text: Like this is, of those going left to right

definitions.text: Like this is, of those going left to right

parts.words: Like this is, of those going left to right
parts.note: among the across clues this one comes third from the end, which is what the word for its position means

explanation.surface: A remark about where this clue stands in a list.
explanation.walkthrough: The across clues run 26, 27, 28, so this clue sits third from last among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means last but two, which is this clue's place in the across list.

clue.text: Rent (gold) returned to Escamillo, perhaps

parts.note: tore is the past tense of tear, so rent

indicators.note: returned means the heraldic word for gold is read backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold handed back to an opera character after a rental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid; it is the past tense of rend. Escamillo is the bullfighter in Bizet's Carmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Escamillo is a bullfighter, an example of the Spanish word for one.

clue.text: Hypercritical officer with evidence of debts

parts.note: Capt is the abbreviation for captain, an officer
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A fault-finding captain with a stack of unpaid notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone captious is quick to find fault over trifles.
